localContext: Hoboken's dense urban landscape, with its proximity to the Hudson River waterfront and mix of historic row houses and high-rise developments, creates unique challenges for wasp and hornet nest establishment. Paper wasp nests appear under eaves and balconies along Washington Street's commercial spaces, while yellow jackets colonize wall voids and attics in the residential neighborhoods near Stevens Institute. The architectural diversity — brick façades, wooden soffits, and older masonry — offers countless entry points for stinging insects seeking protected nesting sites.
